title: Why scale the attention scores
summary: What the sqrt(d_k) divisor is doing before the softmax.

choices.text: Each head's output sums d_k terms, so its variance grows with d_k; dividing the scores keeps the residual stream's variance from growing with the head size.
The dot product of two such vectors has variance about d_k. Dividing by sqrt(d_k) keeps the logits near unit scale, where the softmax still has a useful gradient.
The divisor turns the dot product into a cosine similarity, so every logit lies in [−1, 1] and the softmax cannot saturate however large d_k gets.
It offsets the softmax denominator, which sums d_k exponentials and would otherwise grow with the head size and push every attention weight toward zero.
